_meta.purpose: Chicken regions (parts). Six regions match master chicken-B. One safety rule covers every part, whole birds, ground chicken and stuffing: 165 F, no rest required by USDA, checked in the innermost thigh and wing and the thickest part of the breast. Everything above 165 F on dark meat is texture preference.
_meta.scores_basis: tenderness 5 = most tender when cooked to its target; richness 5 = fattiest (thigh, wing skin). Editorial.

regions.name: Breast
regions.short_description: Lean white meat. 165 F is both the safety minimum and the practical ceiling; past it, it dries.
regions.long_description: FSIS lists breast halves bone-in (6 to 8 oz) and boneless (4 oz) with grilling planning times of 10 to 15 and 6 to 8 minutes per side. Brining or a marinade in the refrigerator helps a lean breast survive the smoker. Higher pit temperatures (325 F and up) keep the skin from going rubbery.

retail_cuts.name: Bone-in, skin-on breast
retail_cuts.note: FSIS planning: 10 to 15 minutes per side on a grill. Thermometer in the thickest part, away from bone.

retail_cuts.name: Boneless, skinless breast
retail_cuts.note: FSIS planning: 6 to 8 minutes per side. Thin end cooks first; probe through the side.

retail_cuts.name: Ground chicken
retail_cuts.note: 165 F like every other chicken product.

regions.planning_time_guidance: FSIS planning times above; a whole bird 60 to 75 minutes indirect. Approximate.
regions.rest_guidance: USDA requires none. 5 to 10 minutes helps juiciness.
common_mistakes: Pulling at 160 F to 'let carryover finish it'. The safety rule is a 165 F reading; carryover is not a safety mechanism.
Judging by colour; FSIS: pink can persist at 165 F.
Washing the raw bird (FSIS: it spreads bacteria).

regions.name: Wing
regions.short_description: Drumette, flat and tip. Skin and fat make it forgiving; the skin needs high heat to crisp.
regions.long_description: FSIS lists wings or wingettes (2 to 3 oz) at 8 to 12 minutes per side on a grill. In a smoker the usual approach is smoke at 275 F then finish hot (400 F or a grill) to crisp the skin. Sauce goes on after cooking or in the last minutes (FSIS: last 15 to 30 minutes for a smoke).

retail_cuts.name: Whole wings
retail_cuts.note: Probe the thickest part of the drumette. Many cooks take wings to 175 F or more for texture; that is preference above the minimum.

retail_cuts.name: Party wings (drumettes and flats)
retail_cuts.note: FSIS planning: 8 to 12 minutes per side grilled.

regions.planning_time_guidance: 1.5 to 2 hours total: about an hour of smoke, then a hot finish. Approximate.
common_mistakes: Low and slow to the end; rubbery skin.
Saucing early and burning the sugar.

regions.name: Thigh
regions.short_description: Dark meat, juicy, forgiving. Safe at 165 F; most cooks prefer it at 175 F or higher, where the connective tissue renders.
regions.long_description: FSIS lists legs or thighs (4 to 8 oz) at 10 to 15 minutes per side on a grill. The thigh is the barbecue chicken cut: enough fat and collagen to sit in smoke for two hours. Bone-in, skin-on thighs are the base of both signature recipes the chicken masters promise.

retail_cuts.name: Bone-in, skin-on thigh
retail_cuts.note: 165 F minimum; 175 to 185 F is the texture preference.

retail_cuts.name: Whole leg (thigh plus drumstick)
retail_cuts.note: Probe the innermost thigh, not touching bone (FSIS).

regions.planning_time_guidance: 1.5 to 2 hours at 275 F smoked; FSIS planning 10 to 15 minutes per side grilled. Approximate. For pulled chicken, take dark meat to 190 to 205 F, probe tender (craft).
common_mistakes: Pulling at 165 F when you wanted rendered dark meat; it is safe but chewy at the joint.
Skin down in a low smoker without a hot finish.

regions.name: Drumstick
regions.short_description: The lower leg. Dark, rich, a handle built in. Same rules as the thigh.
regions.long_description: FSIS lists drumsticks (4 oz) at 8 to 12 minutes per side on a grill. Tendons run the length of the bone; cooking past 165 F toward 180 F softens them, which is why drumsticks are rarely served at the bare minimum.

retail_cuts.name: Drumsticks
retail_cuts.note: Probe alongside the bone, not touching it. FSIS planning: 8 to 12 minutes per side grilled.

regions.planning_time_guidance: 1.5 to 2 hours at 275 F. Approximate. For pulled chicken, take dark meat to 190 to 205 F, probe tender (craft).
common_mistakes: Probe touching bone reads high and fools you into pulling early.

regions.name: Back
regions.short_description: The backbone and frame. Little meat, deep flavour: stock, and the piece you remove to spatchcock.
regions.long_description: Spatchcocking (removing the backbone and flattening the bird) is the method that makes a whole smoked chicken cook evenly; FSIS's whole-bird rule still applies, 165 F in the innermost thigh and wing and the thickest breast. Roast the back for stock.

retail_cuts.name: Back / carcass
retail_cuts.note: Stock and soup. Refrigerate within 2 hours; use in 3 to 4 days (FSIS).

retail_cuts.name: Whole chicken (spatchcocked or trussed)
retail_cuts.note: FSIS planning: broiler-fryer 3 to 4 lb, 60 to 75 minutes indirect on a grill, 1.25 to 1.5 hours roasted at 350 F. Check thigh, wing and breast.

regions.planning_time_guidance: Whole bird 60 to 75 minutes indirect (FSIS planning); spatchcocked at 325 to 350 F, roughly an hour. Approximate.
regions.slice_direction: Joint the bird; slice the breast across the grain.
common_mistakes: Stuffing a bird ahead of time (FSIS: stuff immediately before cooking, and the stuffing must also reach 165 F).
Trusting the pop-up timer over a thermometer.

regions.name: Tail
regions.short_description: The parson's nose. A small, fatty morsel; smoked, it is a cook's treat, or it goes in the stockpot.
regions.long_description: Included because the diagram numbers it. There is no separate FSIS rule; it is poultry, 165 F.

retail_cuts.name: Tail
retail_cuts.note: Sold in bulk in some markets; otherwise part of the whole bird.
